correctness.rationale: The product-character generating polynomial gives the degree-one and degree-two sums. Strict bounds 2<R(p)<3 give the change in adjacent multipliers and a unique maximizing shell, including q=3. Direct endpoint bounds and A_*=-B_*≥0 give the strict crossing, and the derivative stays positive past p=1. Double-centering and Schoenberg's criterion give the stated positive-exponent consequences; the p=0 discrete convention also gives a positive Gaussian kernel when separately included. Expanding the exact multiplier at p=O(1/n) gives the displayed periodic coefficient and the derivative of order n gives the O_q(n^-3) root error. A binomial local limit gives the nullspace fraction. Independently replayed with `python3 /workspace/reviews/evidence/reproduce.py 2` (444 coefficient and shell test cases and the q=n=4 example); finite checks supplement the proof. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed.
